column1: daredevil§The daredevil crossed the gorge on a cable in 1859, and three men who tried to copy him that year died.§这位**冒险家**在 1859 年靠一根钢索横越峡谷，同年三名效仿者丧了命。§dare（敢）+ devil（魔鬼）→ 敢跟魔鬼叫板
daunt§The size of the archive daunted every graduate student except one, who simply started at the first box.§档案的规模**吓住**了除一人之外的所有研究生，那人只是从第一个箱子开始翻。§
deadly§The most deadly stretch of the road is also the straightest, which surprises everyone until they see the speed data.§这条路**最致命**的一段恰恰是最直的一段，人们看到车速数据前都觉得意外。§
deafen§The machinery deafened two generations of workers before anyone thought to measure the noise it made.§这些机器**震聋**了两代工人，才有人想到去测量它们的噪音。§
dearth§A dearth of trained inspectors, not a shortage of rules, explains why the same violations recur every year.§解释同样的违规为何年年重演的是训练有素的检查员**匮乏**，而不是规则不够。§
debacle§The launch was a debacle: the site went down in nine minutes and stayed down for the rest of the day.§这次上线是一场**溃败**——网站九分钟内瘫痪，剩下一整天都没恢复。§
debase§Repeated pardons debased a mechanism that had once been reserved for genuine injustice, and nobody now takes it seriously.§一再的赦免**贬损**了一项本来只留给真正冤情的机制，如今没人再拿它当回事。§de-（向下）+ base（低）
debatable§Whether the policy worked is debatable; whether it was ever properly funded is not.§这项政策是否奏效**尚可争论**，它是否得到过足额拨款则毫无疑问。§
debilitate§Six months of bed rest debilitated her far more than the illness itself had.§六个月卧床**使她衰弱**的程度远超疾病本身。§de-（去掉）+ bil（力量，同 ability 能力）
debunk§A single graduate student debunked the claim by repeating the experiment with the control the original had omitted.§一名研究生**戳穿**了这一说法——他重做实验，加上了原实验漏掉的对照组。§de-（去掉）+ bunk（胡话）

deceit§The deceit was small and the consequences were not: one altered date moved the whole liability to another company.§这次**欺骗**很小，后果则不然——改动一个日期就把全部责任转到了另一家公司。§de-（离开）+ ceit ← cap（拿，同 capture 捕获）→ 把人诓走
deceitful§The most deceitful sentence in the brochure is technically true, which is precisely why the regulator could do nothing.§这本手册里最**欺骗性**的一句在技术上是真的，这正是监管方无可奈何的原因。§
deceive§The graph deceives without lying: the axis starts at ninety, so a two-percent change fills half the page.§这张图不撒谎却能**欺骗**——纵轴从九十开始，于是百分之二的变化占了半页。§
decimation§The decimation of the flock took one winter, and the breeders spent nine years rebuilding what was lost.§羊群的**大批死亡**只用了一个冬天，育种者花了九年重建失去的一切。§decim（十分之一，同 decimal 小数）→ 罗马军中每十人杀一人
decipher§Nobody could decipher the notebook until someone noticed the writer had simply reversed every line.§没人能**破译**这本笔记，直到有人注意到作者只是把每一行都反着写。§de-（去）+ cipher（密码）
decisive§The decisive factor was not the argument but the calendar: the vote fell three days before an election.§**决定性的**因素不是论辩而是日程——投票赶在大选前三天。§de-（完全）+ cis（切，同 scissors 剪刀）→ 一刀切定
decode§Machines can decode the signal in milliseconds; understanding what the sender meant still takes a person.§机器能在毫秒内**解码**信号，理解发送者的意思仍然需要人。§
decorative§The columns are purely decorative: they carry no load, and removing them would change nothing but the view.§这些柱子纯属**装饰**——不承重，拆掉除了景观什么也不改变。§
decorous§Her decorous refusal was so smoothly done that the host did not realize he had been turned down.§她**得体的**拒绝做得如此顺滑，主人竟没意识到自己被回绝了。§decor（合宜，同 decorate 装饰）
decorum§Decorum kept the meeting civil and kept the actual disagreement entirely off the record.§**礼仪**让会议保持了体面，也让真正的分歧完全没有进入记录。§
decry§Economists decried the tariff for a decade, and it survived four governments that had promised to remove it.§经济学家**抨击**这项关税十年，它却熬过了四届承诺取消它的政府。§de-（向下）+ cry（喊）→ 喊着贬低
defective§One defective batch reached eleven countries before the fault was traced to a single machine in one plant.§一批**有缺陷的**产品流到十一个国家，才把故障追溯到某厂的一台机器。§de-（离开）+ fect（做，同 perfect 完美的）→ 没做到位
defense§The best defense in the file is procedural: the search was authorized by a warrant that named the wrong address.§卷宗里最好的**辩护**是程序性的——搜查所依据的令状写错了地址。§de-（离开）+ fens（打，同 offend 冒犯）→ 打退来犯
defensive§He turned defensive the moment anyone asked for numbers, which convinced the board faster than the numbers would have.§一有人要数据他就变得**防卫性十足**，这比数据本身更快说服了董事会。§
defer§The committee deferred the decision four times, and the option it was deferring expired in the meantime.§委员会四次**推迟**决定，而被推迟的那个选项在此期间过了期。§de-（离开）+ fer（带，同 transfer 转移）→ 往后挪
deferential§His deferential manner with senior colleagues vanished entirely when he spoke to anyone junior.§他对资深同事**恭敬**的做派，一对上资历浅的人就消失得无影无踪。§
deferment§The deferment lasted eleven months, by which point the funding it protected had been reallocated elsewhere.§这次**延期**持续十一个月，那时它所保护的经费已被调拨他处。§
defiant§She remained defiant through the hearing and apologized only after reading the transcript six months later.§整场听证她都**桀骜不驯**，六个月后读了笔录才道歉。§de-（离开）+ fi（信任，同 fidelity 忠诚）→ 不再效忠
deficient§The diet was deficient in one vitamin, and that single gap produced symptoms doctors spent years misreading.§这种饮食**缺乏**一种维生素，仅此一项空缺就产生了医生多年误读的症状。§de-（离开）+ fic（做）→ 做得不够
deficit§The deficit was covered by a reserve fund that had been built for exactly this and never used before.§这笔**赤字**由一项专为此设立、此前从未动用的储备金填补。§
definable§The category is barely definable, which has not stopped three agencies from writing regulations that depend on it.§这个类别几乎**无法界定**，这并未阻止三家机构制定依赖它的规章。§
define§How you define "employee" decides who gets sick pay, and four million people sit on the wrong side of that line.§你如何**定义**「雇员」决定了谁能拿病假工资，而四百万人落在这条线的另一边。§de-（完全）+ fin（边界，同 finish 结束）→ 划出界限
definitive§No definitive edition exists: the author revised the text four times and left no instruction about which to prefer.§不存在**权威定本**——作者修订过四次，也没留下该以哪一版为准的说明。§
deflect§A steel plate deflected the fragment, and the operator walked away from an accident that should have killed him.§一块钢板**偏转**了碎片，操作员从一场本该致命的事故中走了出来。§de-（离开）+ flect（弯曲，同 reflect 反射）
defunct§The society is defunct, though its bank account remains open and quietly collects interest nobody claims.§这个学会已**不复存在**，可它的银行账户仍开着，悄悄收着无人认领的利息。§de-（离开）+ funct（履行，同 function 功能）→ 不再运作
defy§The little press defied an injunction, printed the article, and stayed in business because the fine was never enforced.§这家小出版社**违抗**禁令印出了那篇文章，罚款从未执行，它便活了下来。§de-（离开）+ fy ← fid（信任）→ 不认你那一套
degenerate§The debate degenerated into a procedural argument, and the substantive question was never put to a vote.§辩论**堕落**成程序之争，实质性问题始终没有付诸表决。§de-（向下）+ gener（种类，同 genus 属）→ 退回劣等
degeneration§Degeneration of the joint was visible on the scan a decade before it began to hurt.§关节的**退化**在扫描片上出现，比它开始疼早了十年。§
degradation§The degradation of the soil took forty years of the same crop and one season to become obvious.§土壤的**退化**用了四十年同种作物耕作，一个季度就变得显而易见。§de-（向下）+ grad（等级，同 grade 等级）
dehydrate§Sunlight dehydrates the fruit in three days, and the flavor concentrates into something the fresh version never has.§阳光三天就把水果**脱水**，风味浓缩成新鲜时从未有过的样子。§de-（去掉）+ hydr（水，同 hydrant 消防栓）
delegate§She delegates everything except the hiring, which she has never once handed to anyone else in twenty years.§除了招聘，她什么都**授权**出去，而招聘这件事二十年来一次也没交给别人。§de-（离开）+ leg（派遣，同 legate 使节）
deleterious§The additive proved deleterious at doses nobody had tested, which happened to be the doses everybody used.§这种添加剂在无人测试过的剂量下被证明**有害**，而那恰是人人使用的剂量。§
deliberate§The omission was deliberate: three drafts contained the figure, and the fourth removed it without a note.§这处遗漏是**故意的**——三份草稿都有这个数字，第四份不加说明地删掉了它。§de-（完全）+ liber（天平，同 libra 磅）→ 反复掂量
deliberation§After nine hours of deliberation the jury asked to see one photograph again and returned a verdict twenty minutes later.§**审议**九小时后陪审团要求重看一张照片，二十分钟后作出了裁决。§
delineate§The report delineates three options and quietly makes two of them impossible in the appendix.§这份报告**勾勒**出三个选项，又在附录里悄悄让其中两个变得不可行。§de-（完全）+ line（线）→ 画出线条
delude§He deluded himself for two years that the numbers would recover, and the numbers had never once recovered anywhere.§他**自欺**了两年，以为数字会回升，而这些数字在任何地方都从未回升过。§de-（加强）+ lud（玩弄，同 illusion 幻觉）
delusion§The delusion was shared, which made it far more durable than any one person could have kept it.§这种**错觉**是共有的，因此比任何一个人独自维持要牢固得多。§
demagogue§The demagogue named an enemy on the first evening and never had to explain a policy for the rest of the campaign.§这位**煽动家**第一晚就点出了敌人，此后整场竞选再不必解释任何政策。§dēmos（人民，同 democracy 民主）+ agōgos（引领）
demanding§The job is demanding in a way the description never suggests: eleven-hour shifts and decisions nobody trains you for.§这份工作的**苛求**是职位说明从未暗示的——十一小时的班，还有无人培训你去做的决定。§
demean§He would not demean the work by pretending it had been easy, and said so in front of the whole department.§他不愿假装这活儿轻松而**贬低**它的分量，并当着全系这么说了。§de-（向下）+ mean（举止／低下）
demise§The demise of the local paper removed the only reporter who had ever attended a council meeting.§本地报纸的**消亡**带走了唯一一位出席过市议会会议的记者。§de-（离开）+ mis（送，同 mission 使命）→ 送走
demographic§The demographic shift was visible in the school roll a decade before it appeared in any official projection.§这一**人口结构**变化在学校名册上显现，比它出现在任何官方预测中早了十年。§dēmos（人民）+ graph（记录，同 graphic 图形的）
demolish§They demolished a building that had stood for two centuries in order to widen a road by four meters.§他们**拆毁**了一栋矗立两个世纪的建筑，只为把一条路拓宽四米。§de-（向下）+ mol（堆／建，同 molecule 分子）
demolition§The demolition took eleven seconds, and the argument about whether to allow it had taken eleven years.§**爆破拆除**用了十一秒，而关于是否允许它的争论用了十一年。§
demonstration§The demonstration failed in front of four hundred people, and the fault turned out to be a loose cable.§这场**演示**在四百人面前失败了，故障原来是一根松掉的线。§de-（完全）+ monstr（显示，同 monster 预兆）
demonstrative§His writing is demonstrative rather than argumentative: he shows you the case and lets you draw the conclusion.§他的文字是**展示性的**而非论辩性的——他把案例摆给你看，让你自己下结论。§
demurral§Her polite demurral was recorded in the minutes as agreement, and she spent a year correcting the record.§她礼貌的**异议**在会议记录里被写成了同意，她花了一年更正这份记录。§de-（离开）+ mur ← mor（拖延）→ 拖着不答应
denial§The denial was categorical, and the documents released three months later contradicted it line by line.§这次**否认**斩钉截铁，而三个月后公开的文件逐行推翻了它。§
denotation§The word's denotation is neutral and its connotation is not, which is why the two sides fight about using it.§这个词的**字面所指**是中性的，其言外之意则不然，所以双方为用不用它而争。§de-（完全）+ not（记号，同 note 笔记）
denounce§Three former colleagues denounced the practice publicly, and all three were unemployed within the year.§三位前同事公开**抨击**这种做法，三人都在一年内失了业。§de-（向下）+ nounc（宣告，同 announce 宣布）
denude§Logging denuded the slope, and the first heavy rain carried the topsoil into the reservoir below.§伐木**剥光**了这道山坡，第一场大雨就把表土冲进了下方的水库。§de-（完全）+ nud（裸，同 nude 裸体的）
denunciation§The denunciation ran two columns and named nobody, which made it impossible to answer and impossible to ignore.§这篇**谴责**占了两栏，一个人名也没点，让人无从回应又无法忽视。§
deny§The agency denies the request in nine cases out of ten, and appeals succeed in about a third of those.§该机构十次中有九次**驳回**申请，而其中约三分之一的上诉会成功。§
dependent§The whole town is dependent on one employer, which is why nobody says publicly what everybody says privately.§整个镇子**依赖**一个雇主，所以人人私下说的话没人公开说。§
depersonalize§Standard forms depersonalize the process, and the family found that the hardest part of the whole month.§标准表格**把过程去人格化**，那家人发现这是整个月里最难受的部分。§
depict§The mural depicts the strike as a festival, which is not how anyone who was there remembers it.§这幅壁画把罢工**描绘**成一场节庆，而在场的人没有一个是这么记得的。§de-（完全）+ pict（画，同 picture 图画）
depletion§Depletion of the aquifer is measured in centimeters a year, and the wells that failed first were the shallowest.§含水层的**耗竭**以每年厘米计，最先干涸的是最浅的那些井。§de-（完全）+ plet（填满，同 complete 完整的）→ 反着说：掏空
